definition: Dot was an iOS AI companion app that chatted with you and remembered context across conversations. It shut down in October 2025.
extendedDescription:
Dot lived on your iPhone as a companion you talked to every day. It remembered what you told it and built on past conversations, which made it feel more personal than a search box.

The app shut down in October 2025, leaving its users to find a new home for the habit. Former Dot users tend to miss two things: the ongoing relationship and the memory of past chats.

Companion apps and productivity assistants solve different problems. A companion keeps you company. An assistant clears your inbox, plans your day, and follows through on tasks.

faqs.answer: Dot shut down in October 2025. The iOS app stopped working and its users had to move elsewhere.
faqs.question: What happened to the Dot app?

faqs.answer: Look for an assistant with real memory across conversations and tools. GAIA is source-available, remembers how you work, and connects to your email and calendar.
faqs.question: Where do former Dot users go now?

howGaiaUsesIt: GAIA keeps the part of Dot people loved, which is memory that builds over time, and adds follow-through. It remembers your preferences and history, then acts on them: drafting replies, scheduling events, and managing tasks across your connected tools.
